title: Generic freeness of finite polynomial modules over a reduced ring
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative reduced ring, meaning that $r^k=0$ for an integer $k\geq1$ implies $r=0$. Let $n\geq0$, put $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and let $M$ be a finitely generated $P$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. For $f\in R$, put $R_f=R[1/f]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] and let $M_f$ be the localization of the underlying $R$-module at $f$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Give $M_f$ its $R_f[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$-module structure with $x_i(m/f^a)=(x_i m)/f^a$. Let $G$ be the union, inside $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], of the principal opens $D(f)=\{\mathfrak p:f\notin\mathfrak p\}$ for which $M_f$ is free over $R_f$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module] and finitely presented over $R_f[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Then $G$ is open and dense in $\operatorname{Spec}R$. Freeness allows an arbitrary, possibly infinite or empty, basis. No Noetherianity, domain hypothesis, nonzero-ring hypothesis, or finite-presentation hypothesis on $M$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 051Z (lemma-generic-flatness-reduced), polynomial-algebra case of the proof: S = R[x_1,...,x_n], for every finite S-module M. Equations equation-flat-and-finitely-presented and equation-good-locus define the good open; the polynomial ring itself is automatically free and finitely presented over R.

proof.text: Write $G_R(N)$ for the good open in the statement. It is open because it is a union of principal opens. If $R=0$, its spectrum is empty and density is vacuous. We prove density by strong induction on $n$, simultaneously for every reduced base ring and every finite module over its $n$-variable polynomial ring. Localizing a finite polynomial module preserves finite generation: the fractions of its chosen generators still generate. A localization of a reduced ring is reduced: if $(a/f^b)^k=0$, then $f^c a^k=0$ for some $c$, hence $(f^c a)^k=0$, so $f^c a=0$ and $a/f^b=0$. The case $n=0$ is included in the cyclic argument below; its constant-relation case supplies the base case.

source.place: Tag 051Z, polynomial case, induction on n; elementary localization and empty-spectrum checks

proof.text: We will repeatedly use the following elementary density assembly. If a dense open $W$ is covered by principal opens $D(h)$ and $G_{R_h}(N_h)$ is dense in each $D(h)$, the localization lemma identifies it with $G_R(N)\cap D(h)$. Every nonempty open $O$ of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ meets $W$, hence meets one of these $D(h)$ in a nonempty open; density there forces $O\cap G_R(N)\ne\varnothing$. Thus $G_R(N)$ is dense. Principal opens form a basis: for $O=\operatorname{Spec}R\setminus V(I)$, the sets $D(a)$, $a\in I$, cover $O$. For any open $V$, the open $V\cup(\operatorname{Spec}R\setminus\overline V)$ is dense, since no nonempty open can lie in $\overline V\setminus V$.

source.place: Tag 051Y (lemma-generic-flatness-locus-reduce), applied via Tag 051X; Tag 051Z, the two dense-open decompositions

proof.text: For this fixed $n$, it suffices to prove density for every cyclic module $P/J$. Indeed, choose generators $m_1,\ldots,m_t$ of $M$ and put $M_i=\sum_{j\le i}Pm_j$. The map $P\to M_i/M_{i-1}$ sending $p$ to $pm_i$ is onto with ideal kernel $J_i$, so $M_i/M_{i-1}\cong P/J_i$. The extension lemma gives $G_R(M_{i-1})\cap G_R(P/J_i)\subseteq G_R(M_i)$. Begin with $G_R(0)=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and induct on $i$. A finite intersection of dense opens is dense: intersect any nonempty open successively with them. This proves the reduction without assuming Noetherianity or finite generation of $J_i$.

source.place: Tag 051Z, cyclic filtration paragraph; Tag 00KZ (lemma-trivial-filter-finite-module), explicit generator filtration; Tag 051W

proof.text: Fix $M=P/J$. Let $I\subseteq R$ be generated by all coefficients of polynomials in $J$, and set $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\setminus V(I)$ and $W=\operatorname{Spec}R\setminus\overline V$. Their union is dense by Step 2. Cover $V$ by $D(a)$ where $a$ is an actual coefficient of some $g\in J$; these cover because a prime containing every such coefficient contains $I$. In $R_a$, this relation has a unit coefficient. Cover $W$ by principal opens $D(h)\subseteq W$. Every coefficient has empty principal open in $\operatorname{Spec}(R_h)$, hence belongs to every prime there. The radical lemma says it is nilpotent; reducedness proved in Step 1 makes it zero. Therefore $J_h=0$ and $M_h=R_h[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, free on monomials and finitely presented over itself. By Step 2, we only need the case that $J$ contains a relation with a unit coefficient. This coefficient-wise cover avoids needing the source's omitted assertion that every element of $I$ is itself a coefficient.

source.place: Tag 051Z, coefficient-ideal reduction, cases (a) and (b); Tag 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology), radical as intersection of primes

proof.text: For a cyclic module with a fixed relation $g=\sum_{K\in E}a_Kx^K\in J$ having a unit coefficient, let $E$ be its nonzero support and $m$ the number of its nonunit coefficients. We prove density by strong induction on $m$, simultaneously over all reduced rings and all such cyclic modules at the fixed $n$. If $m=0$ and $g$ is constant, its coefficient is a unit, so $J=P$ and $M=0$; the good open is the whole spectrum. When $n=0$, every polynomial is constant, so these reductions already settle the base of the outer induction. Empty spectra encountered after localization have already been settled in Step 1.

source.place: Tag 051Z, induction on m and constant-unit case, including n=0

proof.text: If $m=0$ and $g$ is nonconstant, necessarily $n>0$. Apply the polynomial-shear lemma: choose positive $e_i$ and put $y_i=x_i-x_n^{e_i}$ for $i<n$, $y_n=x_n$. These are polynomial coordinates since the inverse is $x_i=y_i+y_n^{e_i}$. The relation becomes $a y_n^d+\sum_{j<d}b_j(y_1,\ldots,y_{n-1})y_n^j$, with $d>0$ and $a$ a nonzero coefficient of $g$, hence a unit. Dividing by $a$, this is monic. Put $A=R[y_1,\ldots,y_{n-1}]$. Modulo $J$, replace every power $y_n^q$ with $q\ge d$ using the monic relation, lowering $q$; it follows by induction on $q$ that $1,y_n,\ldots,y_n^{d-1}$ generate $P/J$ over $A$. The outer induction now applies to this finite $A$-module.

source.place: Tag 051Z, m=0 nonconstant case; Tag 051N (lemma-helper-polynomial), triangular substitution and monic relation

proof.text: On the dense good open furnished by the outer induction, every point has a principal neighbourhood $D(f)$ where $M_f$ is free over $R_f$ and finitely presented over $A_f=R_f[y_1,\ldots,y_{n-1}]$. The polynomial ring $P_f=A_f[y_n]$ is a finite type $A_f$-algebra, generated by $y_n$. The finite-type-subring lemma therefore makes $M_f$ finitely presented over $P_f$ as well. The triangular coordinate isomorphism fixes $R_f$ and identifies this with the original polynomial action; transporting a finite generator-and-relation presentation along that ring isomorphism preserves its exactness and finiteness. These principal opens are contained in $G_R(M)$, which is therefore dense. This completes the inner base case $m=0$ for $n>0$.

source.place: Tag 051Z, m=0 paragraph, passage back to the original polynomial ring; Tag 0561 (lemma-finitely-presented-over-subring) supplies precisely the finite-presentation direction needed

proof.text: For $m>0$, choose a nonunit coefficient $a=a_K$ of $g$. Partition a dense open as $D(a)\cup(\operatorname{Spec}R\setminus\overline{D(a)})$. On $D(a)$ the coefficient $a$ becomes a unit. On each principal open $D(h)$ contained in the other piece, $D(a/1)$ is empty in $\operatorname{Spec}(R_h)$; the radical lemma and reducedness imply $a/1=0$. In both cases the localized relation still has a unit coefficient unless the spectrum is empty, already handled. Previously unit coefficients remain units, and in the second case the chosen nonunit leaves the support. Thus the number of nonzero nonunit coefficients strictly drops in each case. The inner induction gives a dense good locus on every such chart; Step 2 and the localization lemma assemble them into density of $G_R(P/J)$. This proves the induction on $m$.

source.place: Tag 051Z, m>0 paragraph and its two localizations; Tag 051X and Tag 00E0

proof.text: Step 4 reduces every cyclic module to the cases proved by the inner induction. Step 3 then proves density for every finite module in $n$ variables. Steps 5 and 7 show that the argument starts at $n=0$ and that the only invocation at fewer variables has $n>0$. Hence strong induction proves the result for all $n$. Openness was established in Step 1. The construction uses neither a finite basis over $R_f$ nor a domain or Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 051Z, end of the polynomial-algebra case, before the general finite-type-algebra reduction

proof_origin.place: Tag 051Z (lemma-generic-flatness-reduced), polynomial-algebra case, both inductions; Tags 051W, 051X, 051N and 0561

Step by step: step 3 builds the filtration from generators and corrects the source's misprint R/J_i to P/J_i. Step 4 covers D(I) by D(a) for actual coefficients a, which replaces the source's 'details omitted' claim, and the W branch uses the radical node plus reducedness to make every coefficient 0. Step 5 sets up the m-induction, and its constant-unit case settles n=0. In step 6 the shear substitution x_i -> x_i + x_n^{e_i} matches y_i = x_i - x_n^{e_i}, and the coefficient a is a unit because m=0. In step 7 the hypotheses of 0561 hold exactly for A_f -> P_f. In step 8 m strictly drops on D(a) and on the complement of its closure. Small cases checked: R=0, n=0, R=k x k, R=Z with Z/2, g=x+2, infinite bases, and a non-reduced k[eps], where the item fails but the helpers stay true.
